footprint.notes: The FY2026 20-F lists Ryanair's 95 operating bases by airport name only, with no country or per-base aircraft, passenger or staff counts. Counting bases per country would mean mapping airports to countries ourselves, so no country rows were made. Employees by country come from the Annual Report 2026's sustainability statement (Table 34, FY26 column; countries with at least 10% of staff: Spain, UK, Italy, Ireland; all others are 'Other', not broken down); the FY26 table gives no date, and the FY25 column matches the March 31, 2025 headcounts. No passengers-by-country or taxes-by-country disclosure was found in the FY2026 20-F or the Annual Report 2026; revenue by country (only where above 10%) is already in the records. The 20-F says the Group opened 3 new bases in FY26. Sites are 12 of the 'principal facilities owned or leased by the Ryanair Group' table in the FY2026 20-F (site area and floor space in square meters, not recorded as values); the same table also lists East Midlands and Krakow (simulator training), Madrid (simulator training and Travel Labs), Travel Labs Wroclaw, and administrative offices in Warsaw, Pieta (Malta) and Vienna. Stansted is now listed as freehold.
